title: Find the fractional variables

blocks.text: A depot-planning MILP decides how many trucks to station at each depot (a whole number, often more than 1) and whether to open each depot (0 or 1). Its LP relaxation has just come back from the solver, and the branch-and-bound loop needs to know which variables are still fractions.
Write `fractional(x, tol=1e-6)` in `fractional.py`. `x` maps each variable's name to its LP value. Return the names of the variables whose value is more than `tol` away from the nearest whole number:
in the order `x` lists them. A value such as 0.9999999 is a whole number that picked up float error, so it is not fractional. Values can be above 1 (truck counts) or below 0 (a change in a count).

from __future__ import annotations


def fractional(x: dict[str, float], tol: float = 1e-6) -> list[str]:

    return []


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(fractional({"open_north": 1.0, "open_south": 0.4, "trucks_north": 3.0, "trucks_south": 2.6}))

the fractional names come back in the order the solution lists them
a value within the tolerance of a whole number, such as 0.9999999, is not fractional
a value above 1 or below 0 is judged by its distance to the nearest whole number

origin.section: A Fractional Value Marks the Variable to Branch On

concepts: a variable is fractional when its LP value is more than a tolerance away from the nearest whole number
